storylines.name: The Iran war that ended with nothing settled: sanctions bluster and the Strait of Hormuz
storylines.note: the strikes never found the uranium, Iran rearmed during the pause and is now being handed toll rights over the strait, so sanctions theater like Bessent's 'financial D-Day' is a bluff he says Washington will never call.

storylines.name: Trump's tariff war and the collapse of the Canada deal
storylines.note: he calls the '$60 billion loss' to Canada five-year-old economics, says Canada should have gone to zero tariffs unilaterally instead of retaliating, and reads the 50% tariffs as cronyism that raises the cost of living Trump promised to cut.

storylines.name: The empty US arsenal and a military being degraded from the top
storylines.note: Patriot and Tomahawk stocks are drained by Ukraine and Iran while Raytheon and Lockheed block competition, and Hegseth's appointees disband drone units and swap electromagnetic catapults for steam.

storylines.name: The $40 trillion debt, surging long yields, and Bessent's attempts to manage them
storylines.note: long rates are rising because investors doubt the debt will ever be repaid, buybacks and yield-curve tricks just move money between pockets, and only spending cuts (entitlements) fix it since revenue is capped near 18% of GDP.

storylines.name: Israel squeezed: withdraw-before-disarm in Gaza, and Turkey as the next flashpoint
storylines.note: he backs Netanyahu's refusal to leave Gaza before Hamas disarms, treats the Syrian air base strike as legitimate preemptive deterrence, and reads the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan pact as Trump handing the region to Islamist powers.

storylines.name: Ukraine defenseless and Russia testing how far it can go
storylines.note: Ukraine has no answer left to Russian ballistic missiles, letting it build Storm Shadow parts itself beats shipping finished weapons, and the CIA director's Moscow trip probably warns Putin off a Baltic probe that a 2021 warning failed to prevent.

storylines.name: AI data centers becoming the thing both parties run against
storylines.note: data centers now poll worse than nuclear plants, Paxton wants criminal liability and Shapiro signed restrictions, and he blames AI companies for fueling the fear instead of making the case.

storylines.name: Democrats' hard-left primary wins: Mamdani, DSA, El-Sayed
storylines.note: the DSA wing keeps taking nominations because it is the only side with conviction, and its actual programs (city supermarkets, rent freezes) produce the opposite of what cost-of-living voters wanted.

storylines.name: Government taking equity stakes and picking industries
storylines.note: about 31 equity deals with no congressional vote, plus subsidies and import bans on Chinese robots, are left-style central planning under a Republican label.

storylines.name: Tucker Carlson building a movement
storylines.note: his ten-point manifesto fuses far-left and MAGA-right around hatred of Israel and of finance, and the Shapiro monologue shows the antisemitic conspiracy underneath; he thinks Tucker running would be more dangerous than Trump.

storylines.name: Trump selling advance access to his own market-moving posts
storylines.note: the $100,000-a-month Truth Social scheme is insider trading in plain sight and impeachable on its own, the latest entry in a pattern he calls the Picasso of corruption.

storylines.name: His new series answering capitalism's popular critics
storylines.note: he has started taking viral critics apart line by line, from Benn Jordan's 'leveragism' to Stanford's new encyclopedia entry on capitalism, because millions hear these claims and no rebuttal.

themes.name: Capitalism versus the mixed economy
themes.angle: we have never had capitalism, only a mixed economy drifting toward statism, and the problems people blame on markets trace to specific government policies.

themes.name: The Trump administration
themes.angle: judged on results, not on which side he is on: not pro-market, not pro-free-speech, and foreign policy is the worst of it.

themes.name: Technology and human achievement
themes.angle: innovation is presumptively good and opposition to it is unearned fear; he ends most shows celebrating what people built this week.

themes.name: Spending, entitlements and the fiscal arithmetic
themes.angle: the deficit is a spending problem, taxes cannot close it, and the gerontocracy transfers wealth from the young because old people vote.

themes.name: Free trade
themes.angle: a tariff is a tax paid at home, and unilateral free trade benefits whoever adopts it no matter what the other side does.

themes.name: Israel, antisemitism and the double standard
themes.angle: Israel is held to a standard Russia and Iran are not, and the loudest attacks on it now come from the populist right as much as the left.

themes.name: Nobody is defending capitalism
themes.angle: the DSA left and the Vance/Tucker right are both statist, so the moral case for markets goes unmade on every platform that matters.

themes.name: Ideas drive history
themes.angle: Marx is the unacknowledged foundation of almost all talk about capitalism, and bad philosophy travels from journals to podcasts to policy.

themes.name: Individual responsibility
themes.angle: companies are liable for force and fraud, not for what people choose to overuse; parents, not platforms or the state, raise children.

themes.name: Art, culture and Objectivism
themes.angle: he judges a work by whether reason and human agency drive it, and notes how completely Rand is left out of serious treatments of capitalism.

themes.name: Art and aesthetics
themes.angle: judge a work on its own terms and by whether reason is the source of the hero's power, not by fidelity or casting rows

themes.name: Debt, deficits, inflation and the Fed
themes.angle: spending is the disease, price rises from supply shocks are not monetary inflation, and stagnation is the likeliest ending

themes.name: Defending capitalism against its critics
themes.angle: the critics never define the word, they leave the entrepreneur out of the picture, and Marx's exploitation story still sits under nearly all of it

themes.name: Free trade and immigration
themes.angle: unilateral free trade pays whoever adopts it, and skilled immigrants grow the pie rather than take a slice of it

themes.name: Technology and AI as human progress
themes.angle: presumptively good and worth defending out loud; the fear is unearned and deregulation, not permission, is the answer

themes.name: The human achievement roundup
themes.angle: rockets, mRNA vaccines, drones and falling battery prices as the standing evidence that free people and markets deliver

themes.name: Tribalism and the crisis of reason on both left and right
themes.angle: woke never left, it changed targets; the vice is caring about loyalty rather than truth, and the right has it too

themes.name: American power abroad
themes.angle: perceived weakness is what invites the next war, from Iran to Taiwan

themes.name: China
themes.angle: genuinely innovative and forward-looking, and simultaneously in real economic trouble

themes.name: Free speech and government power over media and speech
themes.angle: an FCC licence review or an FTC bias rule is censorship whichever party writes it

themes.name: Objectivist ethics: altruism against self-interest
themes.angle: the moral premise, not ignorance, is what keeps people reaching for socialism

themes.name: Personal responsibility against corporate liability
themes.angle: force and fraud are the only grounds for blame; parents, not platforms, raise children

themes.name: Tribalism and the collapse of reason
themes.angle: woke never died, it changed target, and the same anti-truth loyalty now runs the right too

themes.name: Trump and the MAGA right
themes.angle: judged on results and on principle, and by that test the right is as statist as the left

moves.main: whatever gets blamed on capitalism, name the specific government policy that actually caused it
secondary: economic power is a trade you can walk away from; political power is the gun
make the critic define the term first, because 'capitalism' and 'leverage' usually dissolve on contact
do the arithmetic before the morality: show the program cannot be paid for, then say it is also wrong
apply the same test to both tribes, and check 'pro-market' or 'pro-free-speech' claims against actions rather than labels
ask who actually pays and who actually benefits, whether it is a tariff, a subsidy or an entitlement
count the unseen cost, not just the visible gain (Bastiat, applied to equity stakes and industrial policy)
put the entrepreneur back in the picture: any account of the economy that omits the producer is broken
hold the policy against its own stated goal and let the contradiction do the work
trace the idea back to its source, from Marx to the seminar room to the podcast
let prices carry the information: a planner overriding the market is claiming to know what the market knows
judge governments by whether they initiate force, not by the good intentions they announce
